trust_decision.summary: Whether a tool/loader-supplied URL may be fetched is decided once by validate_url (scheme + DNS-resolved private/reserved IP check) on the initial URL only; requests.get then follows 3xx redirects to any host unchecked. The fix adds safe_get, which re-validates each redirect hop and strips credentials on cross-origin hops.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'scraping fetches'; ScrapeWebsiteTool is the canonical scraper and shows validate_url immediately followed by requests.get with default redirect following.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/rag/loaders/utils.py:37 (load_from_url, shared by csv/json/xml/mdx loaders, e.g. lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/rag/loaders/csv_loader.py:16); also pdf_loader.py:50, docx_loader.py:46, docs_site_loader.py:29, webpage_loader.py:28 under lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/rag/loaders/

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RAG loaders look already protected: RagTool.add calls validate_url on every http(s) source before any loader runs (lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/rag/rag_tool.py:311-317), and they live under rag/loaders, not the scraping tools the report names; for O8, Selenium is a real browser whose redirects requests-level code cannot intercept, and Serply news links come from a trusted search API, not the user.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate redirects must keep working: relative Location headers (urljoin), same-origin redirects keep Authorization/cookies, cross-origin public redirects are followed with credentials stripped, chain capped at max_redirects; also the CREWAI_TOOLS_ALLOW_UNSAFE_PATHS escape hatch must still bypass. A fix that sets allow_redirects=False everywhere or strips all headers breaks scraping of sites that redirect http->https or to /final.

O6_input_shapes: multi-hop redirect chains, capped by max_redirects (fix.diff:196-198)
credentials passed as headers dict (Authorization, Cookie, X-API-Key, *token*/*secret* names) and as cookies kwarg, stripped only on cross-origin hop (fix.diff:142-176, fix.diff:211-212)
callers with and without explicit headers/cookies/timeout kwargs (fix.diff:22, fix.diff:47, fix.diff:238-241)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SeleniumScrapingTool fetches agent-supplied URL in a local browser with only an http(s) regex, no validate_url on the URL or on redirects
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Browser-driven transport, not requests; redirects (and JS navigation) cannot be checked per hop, and the tool never had validate_url, so it reads as a separate feature outside a 'redirect bypass' fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different tool subpackage (tools/selenium_scraping_tool) from landing point; same crewai-tools package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SerplyNewsSearchTool follows each search-result link with requests.get (redirects on) without validate_url
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Link URLs come from the Serply API response rather than the user/agent, and the tool is a search tool, not a scraper.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different tool subpackage (tools/serply_api_tool); same crewai-tools package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a HEAD/content-type probe (requests.head with allow_redirects=True) before download to detect PDF vs HTML
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Loaders already guess type from URL; a maintainer adding content sniffing would naturally use requests.head with redirects, bypassing safe_get.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: crawl the relative nav links found on the docs page (urljoin + requests.Session().get) to load subpages
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The loader already collects and urljoins nav links for 'Related documentation pages'; fetching them is the obvious next feature and a session-based fetch would not go through safe_get.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a direct-fetch fallback (requests.get(url)) when r.jina.ai fails or no API key is set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Fallback-on-error to a plain fetch is a common pattern; it would keep validate_url-then-requests.get, i.e. the pre-fix shape.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918) via unvalidated HTTP redirect following, plus credential forwarding across origins
